details: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting, released on October 7, 2026, indicate that most policymakers anticipate another interest rate hike by year-end to combat elevated inflation. However, market probabilities for an October 28 rate hike remain low (16-18%), favoring a hold, with expectations shifting towards a December increase. A crucial data point, the September 2026 Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, is scheduled for release on October 14, 2026, and will heavily influence the Fed's next moves.
title: Fed Minutes Hint at More Hikes, CPI Looms Large for October Decision

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) is expected to pause its interest rate hikes at the upcoming October 29, 2026, meeting. Minutes from the September meeting, released on October 8, 2026, confirmed unanimous support for the prior 25 basis point hike due to inflation concerns. However, the minutes also suggested that further rate increases could negatively impact economic growth in the eurozone. Market pricing indicates an 86-91.5% probability of a hold on rates, signaling a potential shift in the ECB's tightening cycle.
title: ECB Likely to Pause Rate Hikes in October, Citing Growth Risks

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has published its October 2026 World Economic Outlook and Global Financial Stability Report, cautioning about the risks associated with "cryptoisation" in emerging markets. The IMF warns that widespread adoption of cryptocurrencies could undermine financial stability and facilitate tax evasion, urging governments to strengthen macroeconomic policies and consider central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) as a response. Additionally, the IMF noted that tokenized markets, while offering efficiency, exhibit lower liquidity and higher volatility than traditional markets, posing potential systemic risks as they grow.
sourceName: International Monetary Fund, LCX Crypto News
title: IMF Highlights "Cryptoisation" Threat and Tokenized Market Volatility

details: On October 7, 2026, US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded net outflows of approximately $487 million, marking the largest single-day outflow in several weeks. Despite this significant outflow, Bitcoin's price remained relatively stable, trading around $82,650-$82,860. Experts noted that such outflows represent shares redeemed by authorized participants, not direct retail selling, and that sustained trends are more impactful than isolated events.
title: US Bitcoin Spot ETFs Experience Largest Outflow in Weeks
